subject.title: Telegram: per-chat lane serialization (isolated ingress) starves messages.queue.collect — same-chat bursts never coalesce

question: Should busy same-lane Telegram spooled updates be admitted into the active followup/collect queue, or should Telegram document `collect` as unavailable for same-chat bursts?
rationale: The source issue is clear, but the fix crosses Telegram spool durability and core followup queue semantics, and scoped Telegram policy requires real transport and replay proof for this class of change.

options.title: Bridge busy-lane updates into collect
options.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that preserves lane ordering and control escapes while allowing same-chat bursts to enter the active followup/collect queue.

options.title: Document unsupported Telegram collect semantics
options.body: Keep current lane serialization and make Telegram same-chat `collect` limitations explicit so users are not promised behavior the transport path cannot currently provide.

options.title: Defer for broader queue redesign
options.body: Leave the issue open as a canonical design item if maintainers want a shared ingress/dispatcher contract instead of a Telegram-only bridge.

recommendation.title: Bridge busy-lane updates into collect
recommendation.body: Implement a Telegram-aware admission path that preserves lane ordering and control escapes while allowing same-chat bursts to enter the active followup/collect queue.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the related followup ordering and recent active-run steering PRs that frame the downstream queue boundary for this decision.
